pr_title: Fix some incorrect SpecialFolder entries for Unix
pr_body:
This PR:
- fixes an incorrect Documents/Personal entry for Linux+Mac (from `HOME` to `XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR`/`HOME/Documents` for Linux and Mac respectively)
- fixes an incorrect Videos entry for Mac (from `HOME/Videos` to `HOME/Movies`)
- fixes an incorrect (Local) ApplicationData entry for Mac (from `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` to `HOME/Library/Application Support` for both ApplicationData and LocalApplicationData)

- Changes the Unix tests to check that `SpecialFolder.Personal` and `SpecialFolder.MyDocuments` are the Documents directory instead of `HOME`.

Fixes #63214, 
Fixes #68323, 
Fixes #40353

issue_context.title: SpecialFolder.MyDocuments / Personal returning wrong path for Unix
issue_context.body:
### Description

Using `Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments)` (and by extensions also `SpecialFolder.Personal`) on Unix based systems does not return the documents folder, and instead returns the same path as `Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.UserProfile)`.

### Reproduction Steps

```cs
Console.WriteLine("Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments:");
Console.WriteLine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments));
Console.WriteLine("Environment.SpecialFolder.UserProfile:");
Console.WriteLine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.UserProfile));
```

### Expected behavior

Since `Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.MyDocuments)` should return the directory that serves as a common repository for documents, it should report the directory I have set via `xdg-users-dir` / `XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR` or `~/Documents` on Mac.

### Actual behavior

It reports my home directory instead.
Comparison between Linux and Windows:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38186597/147738201-09956fdf-9a5a-413b-b18a-b0030fa88b53.png)

Checking [this](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/af9202a6daf91ba58d5d58bafbb6581aebb8a642/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Environment.GetFolderPathCore.Unix.cs#L89) it seems that it's intentional. Why doesn't it just use `ReadXdgDirectory(home, "XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR", "Documents");` there? I can do a PR if it's wished for.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

Dotnet version: 6.0.101
Can reproduce on the following distros: Arch Linux WSL2, Ubuntu 20.04 WSL2, Arch Linux, macOS Big Sur
Architecture: x64



### Other information

_No response_

For Linux, the only question is whether this would be a breaking change for anyone who has XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR set, but prefers/expects `/` or whatever home is. I think this is a reasonable change to make in a major version as the intent is clear (as is the workaround)

For macOS, looking at their [list of user folders](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/FileSystemProgrammingGuide/FileSystemOverview/FileSystemOverview.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40010672-CH2-SW2) the code is not just missing Documents (returning just home) but also should be returning Movies (not 'Videos'). Hmm, I found discussion in https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/12575 expressing these concerns. It seems a little odd though, as it only affects systems that have XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR explicitly set. Do you know how that is typically set? Do users configure it, or is it preconfigured? If the former, one would think we'd be following their intent.

> Do you know how that is typically set?

XDG user directories are usually set in `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/user-dirs.dirs` (and `/etc/xdg/user-dirs.dirs`, but that behaves slightly differently).
Any Desktop Environment that's XDG compliant (which is to say most of them) will create the file and fill it out with appropriate values. This is how an example configuration can look like:
```
XDG_DESKTOP_DIR="$HOME/Schreibtisch"
XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR="$HOME/Dokumente/"
XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$HOME/Downloads"
XDG_MUSIC_DIR="$HOME/Musik"
XDG_PICTURES_DIR="$HOME/Bilder"
XDG_PUBLICSHARE_DIR="$HOME/"
XDG_TEMPLATES_DIR="$HOME/"
XDG_VIDEOS_DIR="$HOME/Videos"
```
Variables that point to the Home directory (i.e. `XDG_TEMPLATES_DIR`) are considered [disabled](https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/xdg-user-dirs/).

If a user wants to use custom directories they can go ahead and edit the file (either manually, via their system settings or with `xdg-user-dirs-update`). Since these aren't actually environment variables, a user could also create an environment variables with that name, which would take priority over the config files. For example, launching `XDG_PICTURES_DIR="~/myTestingFolder" ./dotnetPrintPicturesDirProgram` would change my pictures directory only for `dotnetPrintPicturesDirProgram` to `~/myTestingFolder` while all other programs would still use `~/Bilder`.

> will create the file and fill it out with appropriate values

Great issue. I'm coming from a [discussion](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/554) also touching the `SpecialFolder` topic, having noticed the irregular behavior as you described aswell:

- Personally backing you here in fixing `MyDocuments` / `Personal` to point to `<home>/Documents` (via `XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR` on Linux) rather than just `<home>`. I suppose this "hickup" happened due to "`Personal`" sounding like the home dir. But given the XML summary already mentioning the Documents folder, its origin being the Windows CSIDL name, and the comment on it in `ShlObj_core.h`...
  ```c
  #define CSIDL_PERSONAL                  0x0005        // My Documents
  #define CSIDL_MYDOCUMENTS               CSIDL_PERSONAL //  Personal was just a silly name for My Documents
  ```
  ...it really should be the "Documents" folder.
Of course, changing this would break code on Linux/macOS assuming other special home folders that are not yet covered in `SpecialFolder` as `Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.Personal), "Downloads")`, for example. But that is an incorrect assumption anyway and where I jump in by properly introducing those folders to `SpecialFolder` in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/554#issuecomment-1107636092, at least for "Downloads" and "Public". And code _really_ needing the user folder should use `UserProfile` anyway.

- Also personally backing you in fixing `MyVideos` to point to `~/Movies` on macOS, and not `~/Videos`, that's just incorrect.

- Additionally, I also noticed that [`XDG` variables are being queried on macOS](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Environment.GetFolderPathCore.Unix.cs#L102) for `Desktop` / `Templates` / `MyVideos`, despite them not existing there.  Since there already is a [preprocessor block](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Environment.GetFolderPathCore.Unix.cs#L110) for special OSX handling, these folders should be queried without XDG and like the others in there.

Since you've already given a lot of thought in fixing the existing `SpecialFolder` paths cross-platform, and I've separately checked the new additions, I suppose it would be great to handle these as separate PRs despite the slightly overlapping topic (given I need an API Proposal for my additions anyway).
@Miepee do you want to offer that PR? I missed your reply earlier.
Yep, I'll do that in a day or two when i get a little more time. Would also, as mentioned above, open a new issue for the other wrong less relevant SpecialFolder mappings.

I hope I don't come along as a showstopper (I want this fix myself :-) ), but dug through related issues, PRs, and API proposals on this, and they make valid points on why this fix was rejected in the past. However, I cannot rate how important the points made are today:

- **2015-09-15** https://github.com/mono/mono/pull/2055
  - rejected as changing `MyDocuments` path would break existing apps
- **2016-10-12** https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/12575
  - rejected as changing `MyDocuments` path would create incompatiblity between Mono and .NET Core
  - alternatively mentions obsoleting problematic enum values and adding new correct ones
    - but enum extensions would break code assuming it maps to CSIDLs on Windows
  - mentions deprecating whole SpecialFolder enum / API in favor of flexible new one
- **2016-10-21** https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/19047 (API Proposal)
  - proposes said API, dropped by proposer due to missing interest
- **2021-12-30** https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/63214 (Issue)
  - this issue, attempting to fix `MyDocuments` path again

(s. also my post at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/554#issuecomment-1107831878)
